study_design_identified: Quantitative analytical cross-sectional household survey (N = 379 farm households) using correlation and simple linear regression, supplemented by narrative reference to secondary government planning documents

study_design_identified: Cluster-randomized revealed-preference field pricing trial (30 villages across 10 sectors in Kigali, N=1,167 enrolled households) paired with a follow-up cross-sectional stated-preference discrete choice experiment (n=157) and provider operational cost accounting
why_tool_chosen: The primary causal/empirical component estimating household demand for improved pit-latrine emptying is a cluster-randomized trial in which 30 villages across 10 sectors of Kigali were randomly assigned at the village (cluster) level to 1 of 12 coupon price/group-discount versions and tracked for real service uptake over 90 days (Sections 2.1, 2.2, and 2.5, PDF p. 3-4, 7). All study components (cluster-randomized revealed-preference trial, follow-up discrete choice survey, and accounting cost model) are quantitative with no qualitative data collection, making the RoB 2 cluster-randomized trials variant the exact matching instrument under RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1.

study_design_identified: Non-randomized comparative longitudinal/panel municipal policy evaluation using urban-area fixed effects, instrumental variables (2SLS and LIML), and spatial econometric (lagged OLS and spatial autoregressive/error MLE) reaction-function models across Brazilian localities (1970-2000)
why_tool_chosen: The study evaluates the determinants and causal population-growth/composition impacts of a decentralized local public policy exposure (municipal under-provision of central piped-water connections to small/informal housing) across competing localities within Brazilian metropolitan areas using comparative panel fixed effects, spatial econometric reaction models, and instrumental variables (2SLS and LIML). Under RISK_OF_BIAS.md Section 1, ROBINS-I is the designated instrument for non-randomized policy/intervention evaluations with a genuine comparator employing IV and comparative longitudinal/panel designs.

study_design_identified: Comparative longitudinal/panel observational study (3,900+ monthly operational records from 2016–2019 across 5 piped water operators in Ghana, Rwanda, and Uganda, analysed via archetype analysis and repeated-measures Generalized Estimating Equations [GEE])
why_tool_chosen: The study is a non-randomized comparative longitudinal/panel evaluation of rural piped water infrastructure and payment interventions—comparing on-premises vs. off-premises connections, prepaid credit meters/ATMs vs. conventional pay-as-you-fetch (PAYF) and monthly billing approaches, and enterprise-led vs. state-led public investment archetypes—using >3,900 monthly panel records (2016–2019) and repeated-measures GEE regression. Under RISK_OF_BIAS.md §1, comparative longitudinal/panel evaluations of policy or service delivery interventions with genuine comparators map directly to ROBINS-I.

study_design_identified: Sequential field experiments comprising (1) a compound-randomized controlled trial of face-to-face tenant engagement (2,584 multi-household compounds) and (2) a two-stage street-cluster-randomized controlled trial of utility service-contract disconnection enforcement (147 street clusters across 4 informal settlements, with second-stage compound randomization within the 73 treatment clusters).
why_tool_chosen: Selected 'RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)' because the focal legal/institutional intervention (contract enforcement via credible disconnection notices and disconnections, evaluated for both utility payment and all 9-month water access, welfare, perception, and rental market outcomes) was randomized across 147 street clusters in a two-stage cluster-randomized design (Sections 5-6, PDF pp. 15-16), and even the companion engagement trial randomized multi-household compounds containing multiple tenant households.

overall_rating: Weak-to-adequate institutional evidence (structured non-validated judgment; adequate multiscale institutional mapping but weak empirical validation due to convenience sampling of N=11 experts, unvalidated binary opinion polling, and absence of empirical outcome measurement)
study_design_identified: Doctrinal-institutional policy and case synthesis (Brazilian rural sanitation law and Ceará SISAR model) combined with a descriptive binary expert-elicitation panel survey (N=11 specialists)
why_tool_chosen: The paper is a doctrinal-empirical hybrid combining narrative institutional/legal analysis of Brazilian rural water governance (Law No. 11.445/2007, Law No. 14.026/2020, Ceará Law No. 162/2016 / SISAR) with a descriptive 11-expert binary ('yes'/'no') strategy-validation survey. It fits none of the six conventional empirical checklists: there is no randomized or non-randomized intervention comparator (ruling out RoB 2 and ROBINS-I), no analytical exposure-outcome dataset or statistical test of association (ruling out JBI Analytical Cross-Sectional and Cohort checklists), no qualitative thematic/transcript analysis despite face-to-face administration of a yes/no form (ruling out CASP Qualitative and MMAT), and no systematic literature search (ruling out AMSTAR 2). Because it does include primary expert-elicitation data alongside statutory/institutional analysis, the Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework is the exact matching instrument rather than NONE.
